title: Integrated Security & Compliance Guidance: RBAC, Auth, Audit Logging, Data Residency, Retention, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's authoritative guidance for security and compliance controls across: RBAC & authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC gates, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and risk/exception handling. It is intended for platform owners, engineering leads, product security reviewers, and compliance auditors.

Goals
- Provide a single reference for applied controls and evidence workflows used during audits (SOC2, ISO27001, GDPR assessments).
- Define minimum standards and responsibilities for engineering teams deploying services (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Describe operational runbooks for security incidents and evidence collection.

Ownership and scope
- Document owner: Security (owner_team: security).
- Operational owner for RBAC/configs: Platform Engineering.
- Audit logging and retention owner: Eng Platform + Security.
- Evidence collection owner: Compliance Program Manager.

1) RBAC & Authentication
Principles
- Least privilege by default. Roles and policies must grant the minimum permissions required for the job.
- Role-based access via central IAM is the canonical source of truth; local ACLs are deprecated except where explicitly documented.
- All privileged access requires MFA and just-in-time elevation where feasible.

Standard Roles (examples)
- PlatformAdmin: manage global infra, billing, and capacity. Requires VP approval for onboarding.
- SecOps: incident response, audit logs access, playbook execution.
- InfraEngineer: deploy/run infra components, manage autoscaling policies.
- ServiceOwner: team responsible for a specific service (deploys, config changes).
- Developer: CI/CD access to non-production environments.
- ReadOnly: view-only access for auditors and analysts.
- CustomerAdmin: for Dedicated/Private customers, scoped to their tenant resources only.

Auth & Provisioning
- Primary SSO: SAML2/OIDC (Okta). SCIM-based provisioning required for all teams; groups map to roles in the platform.
- MFA (TOTP or hardware key) required for all interactive logins.
- Service-to-service auth: short-lived mTLS certificates or OAuth2 client credentials with scoped scopes; no long-lived static keys.
- Token lifetimes: interactive session tokens expire after 12 hours; service tokens are short-lived (default 15 minutes) with automated rotation.
- Secrets: stored in KMS-backed vault (AWS KMS / HashiCorp Vault for private deployments). Secrets in source code are prohibited and scanned by CI.

Access Review cadence
- Quarterly automated access reviews via SCIM sync and audit reports.
- Any PlatformAdmin or SecOps onboarding requires documented justification and 2 approvers.

2) Audit Logging
What we log (minimum)
- Identity/auth events: login, SSO failures, token issuance/revocation, role elevation.
- Administrative actions: role changes, policy edits, billing/quotas modifications.
- Data plane events: model loads/unloads, model version rollouts, inference requests metadata (no full request bodies unless approved).
- Configuration changes: infra deployments, config drift, IaC apply events.
- Incident actions: containment steps, escalation notes, evidence snapshots.

Log sinks and availability
- Hosted: primary logs to AWS CloudWatch + replicated to BigQuery for analytics and long-term retention.
- Dedicated/Private: logs are written to customer-designated sinks; we provide configuration templates for regional endpoints.
- Availability SLO: audit log write success >= 99.99% (measured per-minute across all active writers).

Retention and retention policy table (summary)
- Authentication logs: default retention 3 years for enterprise customers; 1 year for standard tenants.
- Administrative change logs (IAM, RBAC): 7 years (compliance evidence default).
- Data plane metadata (inference telemetry): 1 year unless customer contract and residency allow longer.
- Full request payloads / PII: stored only with explicit customer consent and additional controls; default is not stored.

Note on PII and redact rules
- PII must be redacted at ingestion using the platform redaction pipeline. Patterns and redaction rules are maintained in the observability repo. Teams must register new sensitive patterns via the security team.

3) Data Residency and Retention (Customer-facing options)
Residency options
- US, EU, APAC region selection at account creation for Hosted or Dedicated. Private deployments default to customer's indicated region.
- All logs and stored artifacts for a given tenancy must remain in the selected region unless explicit legal approval is obtained.

Default retention by data type (examples)
- Billing & usage: 7 years (US/EU local store).
- Audit & admin logs: 7 years for customers under enterprise contract; otherwise 1-3 years.
- Model artifacts (non-sensitive): lifecycle per customer policy; default 90 days unless pinned.

Cross-border and legal holds
- Legal holds override retention. Requests for legal holds must be routed to Legal@redwood.com and SecOps; evidence preservation is handled by Compliance and SecOps.
- For customers requiring strict in-country residency, we operate regional object stores and replication is disabled unless permitted.

4) Secure SDLC Requirements
Gates and tooling (must be enforced by CI/CD pipelines)
- Code review: all PRs require at least one peer review and one security reviewer for services with high-privilege scope.
- Static Analysis (SAST): runs on every PR; failure blocks merge.
- Dependency scanning (SCA): alerts for critical/known-vulnerable dependencies; auto-block for CVSS >= 9.0.
- Secrets detection: pre-commit and CI scanning; any detected secret blocks merge and triggers rotation.
- DAST / Runtime checks: scheduled for production-facing services quarterly.
- Threat modeling: required for new components that handle customer data, authentication, billing, or model execution.

Deployment and rollout controls
- Canary and progressive rollouts for model-serving components with automated rollback on error thresholds (5xx rate > 1% or latency p95 increase > 50% within 10m).
- Privileged config changes require a two-person approval in the deployment system and change record in the infra change log.

Secure build artifacts
- All production images must be signed and provenance recorded in the artifact registry. Rebuild reproducibility notes must be available for auditors.

5) Incident Response — Security Procedures
Quick reference (high level)
1. Detect: security tooling, monitoring, or user report triggers an alert in PagerDuty SecOps.
2. Triage: SecOps lead classifies severity (P0/P1/P2) and assembles response team.
3. Contain: apply immediate mitigations (network ACLs, revoke compromised keys, isolate nodes).
4. Preserve evidence: snapshot disks, export audit logs to an immutable store, capture memory images when required, and record chain-of-custody in the incident ticket.
5. Remediate: deploy fix and validate via canary.
6. Communicate: internal stakeholders and affected customers (per SLAs) using the communications playbook.
7. Post-incident review: produce a security postmortem with root cause, timeline, impact, and action items.

Forensics and evidence handling
- Preserve original logs and prevent tampering: write-once storage or WORM-enabled buckets for evidence exports.
- Forensic snapshots must include: list of affected hosts, time-synced logs, API tokens active at time of incident, deployment manifests, and network flow captures where available.
- Documentation: every evidence item must be recorded in the incident ticket with owner, acquisition time, and storage path.

Escalation thresholds
- P0: data exfiltration or production control-plane compromise — immediate Exec notification and legal/PR engagement.
- P1: service compromise with potential customer impact — SecOps + CTO briefing within 1 hour.
- P2: suspected intrusion with no confirmed data access — SecOps investigation within 4 hours.

Communication templates
- Internal: incident standup agenda, decision log, action owner list.
- External (customer): concise notice with impact, scope, mitigation steps, and expected timeline. Legal approves customer notice for incidents that may affect contractual obligations.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows
Evidence types and owners
- Configuration evidence (IaC manifests, access lists): ServiceOwner (maintains manifests), PlatformEngineering (exports snapshots).
- Access evidence: IAM change logs and quarterly access review reports — SecOps owner.
- Operational evidence: runbooks, SLO reports, incident postmortems — ServiceOwner + SRE.

Automated collection
- Evidence collector agents run weekly to snapshot policy docs, IAM policies, audit logs indices, and signed build artifacts into the evidence repo (BigQuery / secure artifact store).
- Each evidence snapshot is tagged with: control_id, captured_at, owner, retention_ttl.

Audit readiness checklist
- Control mapping file (control_id -> evidence artifacts) maintained by Compliance.
- Evidence gap run executed monthly; assigned owner must remediate within 10 business days or file a risk exception.

7) Risk and Exceptions
Exception request process
1. Submit exception request via internal exception form (link provided in related pages). Form fields: control_id, justification, compensating_controls, risk_owner, expiration_date.
2. Risk committee review: Weekly triage. High-risk exceptions require Security Director approval and a mitigator plan.
3. Compensating controls: increased monitoring, stricter segmentation, additional audit sampling.
4. TTL and review: exceptions granted for a maximum of 90 days (unless renewed) and must include measurable acceptance criteria.

Monitoring and sunset
- All active exceptions published to a monthly compliance dashboard. Exceptions without remediation after two review cycles are escalated to the CTO.
